text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall for incidents@redwood — high error rate detected on serving-runtime cluster gpu-swarm-7, potential multi-GPU communication failures (nccl) — trace_id=rt-9a3f

morgan: saw alerts from the runtime dashboard, latency spiking and ~30% of TP jobs are stuck in STEP_WAIT. GPU telemetry shows repeated Xid 79 from node gpu-swarm-7a.

lee: confirmed, getting repeated `NCCL: unhandled cuda error` in logs for several tensor-parallel processes. Also seeing container restarts on that node.

sanjay: copying key logs here (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T04:12:03Z Runtime ERROR: ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled cuda error
[pid 1423] Xid (79) GPU fault on GPU 2, process pid=1423
container: /var/lib/containers/cc792/restart(1)
```

morgan: looks like an OOM triggered a GPU fault, but the pattern is cross-process (communicator resets). Node flaps — likely a driver/kernel intermittent issue. We should isolate the node.

ops-bridge-bot: Bridge created — incident-bridge-4071234567 (https://meet.redwood/bridge/4071234567)

morgan: immediate plan: 1) cordon & drain gpu-swarm-7a 2) reroute new TP jobs to fallback pool (gpu-fallback-2) 3) restart impacted containers with debug flags and collect core dumps 4) notify customers impacted. Can infra take the drain? @infra-eng

infra-eng: starting drain now. Command: `kubectl cordon gpu-swarm-7a && kubectl drain gpu-swarm-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — ETA ~3m to evict running pods.

lee: while drain runs, run `nvidia-smi -q -d PIDS,FAULTS` and collect dmesg from the node. Also capture `nvidia-bug-report.sh`.

tara-support: I’ll open a customer-facing blurb for affected tenants: short note saying we’re investigating multi-GPU failures, jobs may be retried automatically and we’re routing to a fallback pool. Will post to status.redwood shortly.

sanjay: heads-up — some long-running TP training jobs will fail when their communicator resets; we should enable automatic retry policy for those job types if not already — there’s a rollout knob in the job controller (policy: `tp_restart_on_comm_error`).

morgan: good call. @lee can you enable temporary controller override to allow up to 2 restarts for existing jobs? Also start capturing KV cache snapshots for affected model shards before containers terminate (if possible).

lee: overriding restart policy: `kubectl patch jobcontroller --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/tp_restart_on_comm_error","value":"2"}]'` — applied. Starting snapshot procedure (may not succeed if communicator already corrupted).

infra-eng: drain completed. Node is cordoned and pods evicted. Attaching logs from machine: `dmesg | tail -n 80` shows multiple GPU faults and a driver reset sequence. Uploading bugreport now.

sanjay: any sign of NVLINK flaps or nv_peer_mem errors? That would indicate fabric-level issues.

infra-eng: nv_peer_mem reports link errors intermittently on GPU1<->GPU2. Not a node-wide fabric outage but localized link resets.

morgan: mitigation status: rerouted new TP traffic to gpu-fallback-2, controller override applied, customers notified draft posted on status.redwood. Support, please add impacted customer list to the incident timeline.

tara-support: posted initial status — "We are investigating GPU communication failures affecting a subset of multi-GPU jobs. Some jobs may be restarted or moved to fallback capacity. We will provide updates within 30 minutes."

ops-bridge-bot: oncall escalation: paging second oncall (sanjay) — acknowledged.

lee: trying a targeted restart of GPU driver on the node after getting infra approval — sequence: `systemctl stop docker && nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 2 && systemctl start docker`. Will only be used on isolated nodes after drain.

infra-eng: we did a controlled driver reset on a spare node to test — worked but exposed kernel traces suggesting a specific kernel module (nv-host) hit a race. File bug against kernel-driver-team.

morgan: tagging kernel team and setting P1 for follow-up. For immediate customer impact: estimate ~12 jobs failed and were retried; 4 customers with long-running training saw progress lost ~1-2 hours. Tara, draft targeted customer pings for those 4.

tara-support: ping templates ready. Sending targeted DMs to customers: includes incident id 4071234567, root cause investigation in progress, workarounds applied (node drain + reroute), ETA for next update 30m.

sanjay: collecting artifacts for postmortem: kube events for involved pods, driver logs, core dumps, NCCL debug outputs in /var/log/redwood/nccl/*.tgz, NV peer logs. Marking all as retained.

lee: quick workaround we rolled out: pin affected jobs to single-GPU fallback variant where possible (degraded performance but avoids multi-GPU comm). This prevented ~20 additional failures during the incident window.

morgan: update: we rolled out an automated fallback rule in router: if nccl errors > 5% within 5m for a pool, route new tensor-parallel jobs to `gpu-fallback-2` for 15m. That will prevent cascading failures during flaps.

ops-bridge-bot: incident update scheduled in 25m. Ensure to attach logs and customer impact summary before that.

infra-eng: collecting dump bundles now, pushing to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/4071234567/ — includes `bugreport.tgz`, `dmesg.log`, `nccl-traces.tgz`.

morgan: next actions before handoff to oncall-2 (tomorrow): 1) Confirm kernel-driver fix plan with kernel team 2) Validate whether we need a hotpatch on other nodes 3) Document fallback policy and automated router thresholds 4) Postmortem timeline and severity classification.

sanjay: adding remediation note: consider bumping autoscaling for fallback pool during early rollback window, and enable proactive health-checks that detect link resets (nv_peer) earlier.

morgan: handing off to followup duty: @infra-eng will own next 6 hours, @sanjay will own postmortem lead, @tara-support will own customer comms. Marking incident as active -> mitigation phase.

infra-eng: acknowledged — will update every 2 hours or on major milestone.

morgan: thanks team. Closing immediate pager; leave thread open for follow-up. :thumbsup:
